A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same prediction-access framework and German unemployment case study. The text, equations, figures, and appendices A–D are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical simulations and analyses of German unemployment records, including CatBoost and decision-tree results in Section 5 and supplementary experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulations, unemployment case-study results, and appendix experiments. These remain original empirical results despite being unchanged from v1.

M1.justification: The screening policy, prediction-access ratio, and residual-scaling procedure are unchanged. CatBoost, the depth-4 decision tree, and the classification formulation already appear in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same German administrative unemployment data for duration prediction and fixed-threshold classification. The Gaussian simulations and evaluated risk-group scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: The CatBoost-versus-depth-4 decision-tree comparison remains unchanged in Figure 8. Figure 6 retains the same constant-prediction, trained-model, and near-perfect-prediction scenarios; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain unemployment spells starting in 2010–2011 for training, 2012 for validation, and 2015 for testing, with outcomes capped at 24 months. Preprocessing, model budgets, metrics, and screening and prediction-improvement settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The training-size and residual-distribution checks in Figures 12–13, prediction-improvement sensitivity analyses, and classification comparison in Appendix B.5 are all retained. No new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and the same point-estimate plots and residual distributions are retained.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged, including test R2 of 0.15, approximately 0.25 additional screening capacity to reach 75% coverage of high-risk jobseekers, and the CatBoost–tree policy-value differences. Appendix results are also retained.

T1.justification: Appendix C's Proposition 4 and its proof explicitly add independence between predictions and errors, correcting an omitted condition in the standalone Gaussian optimality statement. Independence was already mentioned in v1's Section 2; the main theorems and Appendix D proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions and claims about prediction as a first- and last-mile effort relative to expanding capacity. The new conclusion summarizes these existing claims without changing their scope.

C2.justification: The expanded Costs passage in Section 1.1 discusses recurring expenses, amortization of fixed investments, and cost-effectiveness over time as unresolved extensions. This develops v1's shorter cost discussion in Section 3.1; interpretations of the empirical findings remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same data provenance, covariates, encoding, CatBoost iteration limit and early stopping, tree depth, and residual-adjustment details. No implementation or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Barocas, Hardt, and Narayanan (2023) and explicit fairness/equity framing. It also expands the comparison with Perdomo (2024), emphasizing its empirical tools alongside the predecessor's theoretical treatment.

P1.justification: v3 moves and expands the cost discussion into Section 1.1, adds Section 6 Conclusion, repairs Definition 2.1's prose, and updates terminology and acknowledgements. Most wording and the overall organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing figures are repositioned relative to surrounding text, notably Figures 2 and 7, with corresponding paragraph and page-layout changes. All 16 figures retain their graphics and display design; none is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 improves formal precision by making Proposition 4's independence requirement explicit and improves exposition through the expanded cost discussion, clearer prior-work comparison, and conclusion. These are useful, localized improvements; the underlying methods and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
